evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.1.92: sī nōn redderet pecūniam, if he would not give back the money
terms.comment: Latin has no word of its own for it: reddere, give back (see give back), with the money as its object; comedy says argentum reddere.

terms.gloss: return a faulty purchase (for the price back); of the seller, take it back
evidence: Plaut. Merc. 419: dīxit sē redhibēre, sī nōn placeat, he said he would take her back if she did not suit
terms.comment: A trader’s word: the goods go back to the seller, and the price to the buyer (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: tū huic argentum redde. hoc jūdicium meum est. — Tū autem in nervō jam jacēbis, nisi mī argentum redditur.
phrases.english: You, give him his money back: that is my judgment. — And you’ll soon be lying in chains if I don’t get my money back.

phrases.latin: sī pāx nōn impetrāta ab senātū foret, obsidēs pecūniamque reddī Philippō receptum est
phrases.english: it was guaranteed that if the senate did not grant peace, the hostages and the money would be given back to Philip

sources: Lewis & Short: reddo · Lewis & Short: redhibeo
